listing.name: VideoLib
listing.summary: Adds a video plugin for Starsector that leverages statically compiled FFmpeg JNI glue code to play videos in the game.

description:
Introducing VideoLib 
A video plugin for Starsector

ChangelogVersion 0.1.0

- Restructured packages. Instead of data.scripts.* it is now videolib.* to be more identifiable

- New feature: AutoTexProjector class

A texture override class designed to run permanently while the game is running for things like animated portraits and illustrations.

Decoder keeps file handle open indefinitely

Has a frame timeout of 2 frames; if the texture is not bound then it will go dormant.

Data driven; see settings.json and the corresponding portrait file for an example usage

You can get a handle on it via VideoPaths.getAutoTexProjectorOverride(key in the settings.json) if you want to pause it or change the video it uses

- Added changelog

- Added version files

- Added actual play/pause/stop "icons" to buttons on control panel

- Added an animated gif portrait for an AutoTexProjector example

- Changed everything to just use RGBA frames instead of selectively using RGBA/RGB24 as simple grug fix for alignment/padding errors resulting from videos with wacky resolutions

- Refactored and cleaned up frame buffer handling

- Fixed freeze related to seeking to end on video player control panel

- Fixed texture uploads rendering upside down without postprocessing

- Fixed crash related to GL unpack alignment when uploading textures with a funky resolution to gpu

- "Fixed" audio drifting progressively behind video on linux (Works on my machine™)

Version 0.1.1

- Added options for AutoTexProjector instantiation to give control over whether or not video frames update for textures during CombatEngine pause

See "campaignRunWhilePaused" and "combatRunWhilePaused" keys in example in settings.json. Defaults to true if not set.

- Various minor AutoTexProjector optimizations

- AutoTexProjectors will now use groups of 50 decoders per thread (maximum can be adjusted in settings.json)

Previously they used a thread for each individual decoder which resulted in many threads competing for java stack heap and used a ton of internal JVM memory.

If there was not much JVM heap headroom it also incurred a non-trivial "juggle" churning cost on the CPU.

This results in a much faster startup time and major reduction in heap usage.

- Reduced AutoTexProjector timeout to 1 frame if its texture is not being rendered

- New GroupedMuteDecoder class RGBATextureBuffer maximum capacity 3 decoded video frames down from 5 (The VideoFrames in system memory, pre-upload to GPU)

- Fixed a minor AutoTexProjector manual control bug

- Renamed some FFmpeg JNI bindings to something more appropriate

- Added an FFmpeg JNI method to (very roughly) estimate passive memory usage of an open FFmpegVideoLibContext struct (i wouldnt trust it tbh)

Version 0.1.1a

- Added a missing (redundant) method for AutoTexProjector that should have been implemented but wasn't

- Fixed a bug with AutoTexProjector changeVideo method where the startUs parameter was ignored

- Fixed a bug with AutoTexProjector setRunWhilePaused method where it had an incorrect signature

- Fixed wrong load op for AutoTexProjector instantiator var6 for the new op that resulted in intermittent JVM hotspot verification failure for the instantiator class

- Some groundwork for audio support for AutoTexProjector (lol), changed MuteDecoderGroup to inherit from abstract class DecoderGroup, moved related classes to "group" sub-package of decoder package[close]

Github Repo

Download

This is a work in progress leveraging statically compiled FFmpeg JNI glue code to play videos in Starsector. It has limited audio support currently. Zero dependencies but you'll probably want console commands.

A video on an InteractionDialogAPI panel with controls

Spoiler[close]

A GIF overriding a RingBand's texture

Spoiler[close]

A VP9 video overriding a Planet object's shieldtex2 field. Note: while it appears to have alpha channel, this one actually does not; black pixels are chroma keyed or something and rendered transparently by Planet objects, though vp8/vp9/gif alpha channel is supported

Spoiler[close]

A multitude of videos without controls playing on a confirm dialog panel

Spoiler[close]

This project includes CustomUIPanelPlugin implementations that render video frames or images as OpenGL textures converted from raw video frames in a ring buffer. As such, it is all rendered natively by the game and

anything you can put a CustomUIPanelAPI on, you can play a video on

, put other UI elements on top or below, use alphamult, etc. Also included are classes to override Planet, Ringband, and Sprite objects' textures, plus a more generalized projector class for any texture in the form of

TexProjector

.

Supports video formats:

mp4

: H264, HEVC

|

webm

: AV1, VP8, VP9

|

Animated GIF

Also includes alpha channel support for VP8 and VP9 if encoded with pixel format

YUVA420P

.

Supports image formats: jpeg, png, gif, webp. Includes alpha channel support for png, gif, and theoretically webp should work with alpha channel also but it is untested.

Idk about systems diagrams or anything but the

VideoPlayerFactory

method parameters are annotated as are the various

PlanetProjector

,

RingBandProjector

,

SpriteProjector

, and

TexProjector

class constructors. For the panel implementation I would recommend using the

VideoplayerFactory

methods. All projector implementations are currently accessible in the videolib.projector package. Refer to the console command implementations for a couple of examples. Video and Image file paths will be resolved relatively via the data/config/settings.json "VideoLib" key in your mod's own settings.json. See the VideoLib's own settings.json for syntax.

There is basic logging for the decoder classes (you cant turn it off unless you recompile with those calls commented out currently), and if seeking with the seek bar then the mode setting logs don't really mean anything. PlayMode setting is kind of irrelevant for the decoder and only its EOFMode really matters anymore, I just didn't bother to clean that up yet.

Important

: Remember to call finish() on projectors (not their decoders, the projector.finish() method will do that) to clean up when done with them, or the decoder thread will be left running and cause a memory leak. For panel projectors if instantiated with the keepAlive parameter as false then they will clean themselves up as soon as they stop advancing. If keepAlive=true then they must be cleaned up manually. Generally UI panel implementations are probably most easily (and should be) created via

VideoPlayerFactory

.

Introducing VideoLib
A video plugin for Starsector
ChangelogVersion 0.1.0

- Restructured packages. Instead of data.scripts.* it is now videolib.* to be more identifiable

- New feature: AutoTexProjector class
    A texture override class designed to run permanently while the game is running for things like animated portraits and illustrations.
    Decoder keeps file handle open indefinitely
    Has a frame timeout of 2 frames; if the texture is not bound then it will go dormant.
    Data driven; see settings.json and the corresponding portrait file for an example usage
    You can get a handle on it via VideoPaths.getAutoTexProjectorOverride(key in the settings.json) if you want to pause it or change the video it uses

- Added changelog
- Added version files
- Added actual play/pause/stop "icons" to buttons on control panel
- Added an animated gif portrait for an AutoTexProjector example

- Changed everything to just use RGBA frames instead of selectively using RGBA/RGB24 as simple grug fix for alignment/padding errors resulting from videos with wacky resolutions
- Refactored and cleaned up frame buffer handling

- Fixed freeze related to seeking to end on video player control panel
- Fixed texture uploads rendering upside down without postprocessing
- Fixed crash related to GL unpack alignment when uploading textures with a funky resolution to gpu
- "Fixed" audio drifting progressively behind video on linux (Works on my machine™)

Version 0.1.1

- Added options for AutoTexProjector instantiation to give control over whether or not video frames update for textures during CombatEngine pause
    See "campaignRunWhilePaused" and "combatRunWhilePaused" keys in example in settings.json. Defaults to true if not set.

- Various minor AutoTexProjector optimizations
- AutoTexProjectors will now use groups of 50 decoders per thread (maximum can be adjusted in settings.json)
    Previously they used a thread for each individual decoder which resulted in many threads competing for java stack heap and used a ton of internal JVM memory.
    If there was not much JVM heap headroom it also incurred a non-trivial "juggle" churning cost on the CPU.
    This results in a much faster startup time and major reduction in heap usage.

- Reduced AutoTexProjector timeout to 1 frame if its texture is not being rendered
- New GroupedMuteDecoder class RGBATextureBuffer maximum capacity 3 decoded video frames down from 5 (The VideoFrames in system memory, pre-upload to GPU)

- Fixed a minor AutoTexProjector manual control bug
- Renamed some FFmpeg JNI bindings to something more appropriate
- Added an FFmpeg JNI method to (very roughly) estimate passive memory usage of an open FFmpegVideoLibContext struct (i wouldnt trust it tbh)

Version 0.1.1a

- Added a missing (redundant) method for AutoTexProjector that should have been implemented but wasn't
- Fixed a bug with AutoTexProjector changeVideo method where the startUs parameter was ignored
- Fixed a bug with AutoTexProjector setRunWhilePaused method where it had an incorrect signature
- Fixed wrong load op for AutoTexProjector instantiator var6 for the new op that resulted in intermittent JVM hotspot verification failure for the instantiator class
- Some groundwork for audio support for AutoTexProjector (lol), changed MuteDecoderGroup to inherit from abstract class DecoderGroup, moved related classes to "group" sub-package of decoder package[close]
Github Repo
Download
This is a work in progress leveraging statically compiled FFmpeg JNI glue code to play videos in Starsector. It has limited audio support currently. Zero dependencies but you'll probably want console commands.

A video on an InteractionDialogAPI panel with controls
Spoiler[close]
A GIF overriding a RingBand's texture
Spoiler[close]
A VP9 video overriding a Planet object's shieldtex2 field. Note: while it appears to have alpha channel, this one actually does not; black pixels are chroma keyed or something and rendered transparently by Planet objects, though vp8/vp9/gif alpha channel is supported
Spoiler[close]
A multitude of videos without controls playing on a confirm dialog panel
Spoiler[close]
This project includes CustomUIPanelPlugin implementations that render video frames or images as OpenGL textures converted from raw video frames in a ring buffer. As such, it is all rendered natively by the game and anything you can put a CustomUIPanelAPI on, you can play a video on, put other UI elements on top or below, use alphamult, etc. Also included are classes to override Planet, Ringband, and Sprite objects' textures, plus a more generalized projector class for any texture in the form of TexProjector.

Supports video formats: mp4: H264, HEVC | webm: AV1, VP8, VP9 | Animated GIF
Also includes alpha channel support for VP8 and VP9 if encoded with pixel format YUVA420P.

Supports image formats: jpeg, png, gif, webp. Includes alpha channel support for png, gif, and theoretically webp should work with alpha channel also but it is untested.

Idk about systems diagrams or anything but the VideoPlayerFactory method parameters are annotated as are the various PlanetProjector, RingBandProjector, SpriteProjector, and TexProjector class constructors. For the panel implementation I would recommend using the VideoplayerFactory methods. All projector implementations are currently accessible in the videolib.projector package. Refer to the console command implementations for a couple of examples. Video and Image file paths will be resolved relatively via the data/config/settings.json "VideoLib" key in your mod's own settings.json. See the VideoLib's own settings.json for syntax.

There is basic logging for the decoder classes (you cant turn it off unless you recompile with those calls commented out currently), and if seeking with the seek bar then the mode setting logs don't really mean anything. PlayMode setting is kind of irrelevant for the decoder and only its EOFMode really matters anymore, I just didn't bother to clean that up yet.

Important: Remember to call finish() on projectors (not their decoders, the projector.finish() method will do that) to clean up when done with them, or the decoder thread will be left running and cause a memory leak. For panel projectors if instantiated with the keepAlive parameter as false then they will clean themselves up as soon as they stop advancing. If keepAlive=true then they must be cleaned up manually. Generally UI panel implementations are probably most easily (and should be) created via VideoPlayerFactory.
aiDescription: It includes CustomUIPanelPlugin implementations to render video frames or images as OpenGL textures, allowing videos to be played on UI panels. The mod also provides classes to override textures for Planet, Ringband, and Sprite objects, along with a generalized projector class for any texture. It supports various video formats like mp4, webm, and animated GIFs, as well as image formats including jpeg, png, gif, and webp.
